title: Lakota Plant Relatives
tagline: What our plant relatives are called, how to say their names, and what they can be for.
intro: Scan a placard in the garden, or choose a plant below, to learn its Lakota name, hear how it is said, and read what it can be used for. If you know something about these plants, please share it with us.
disclaimer: This webpage is for informational purposes only and is not intended as medical advice. The authors and contributors assume no liability for any allergy, illness, injury, or other adverse effects resulting from the use of this information or the plants discussed.
credits:

Recipes and stories are courtesy of our wide community of passersby. Share yours on any plant page.

Some uses draw on [Linda Black Elk's testimony to the South Dakota Public Utilities Commission (PDF)](https://puc.sd.gov/commission/dockets/HydrocarbonPipeline/2014/HP14-001/testimony/betest.pdf).
share_blurb: Do you know a use, a story, or a recipe for one of these plant relatives? Share it here. We read everything, and we may add it to the page with credit to you.
language_blurb: If you know these plants by another name in your language, please tell us. We would love to add it to the site, with credit to you and your nation.
